items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'Sound good?' confirmation
Never asked for a box count (customer volunteered it)
Never listed what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools)
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee never stated (arrival windows only)
Number of movers and trucks never stated
No 'does that make sense?' close on the prep speech
Bolded email detail list never mentioned
No 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
No 'any other questions before I let you go?'
top_strength: Outstanding discovery and consultative estimating. Chris ran a genuinely thorough room-by-room inventory, chased the access detail others skip ("from where we can park our truck to your door about how far the walk in fee our yards"), and turned the bed frame into a real cost conversation by pricing the labor honestly: "I've seen tear down you know thirty minutes to 45 minutes put backup usually there's a little bit longer." He then modeled the estimate three ways across day-of-week tiers so a price-sensitive customer could self-select, and volunteered the efficiency coaching unprompted enough to earn Save Your Ass. The rapport was real - the customer closed with "Thank you so much Chris. I really appreciate you."
coaching_note: The differentiators never got said. On a 26-minute call Chris covered rate, day tiers and disassembly but skipped No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee and the no-hidden-fees pitch entirely - and the miss is expensive here, because this customer explicitly asked for a price break ("Do you all happen to have any discounts for like different companies") and got only "No, unfortunately we don't." That was the moment to sell value instead of conceding on price. Damage coverage was especially glaring: he asked her to sign a liability waiver for the bookshelf without ever explaining the $2,000 No Worries coverage that sits behind it. Build a 60-second differentiator block and run it every call right after the hourly rate.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and natural - he matched her energy on the rent-increase venting ("every, every bit counts"), joked along on the collapsing bookshelf, and she closed by thanking him by name, though long stretches of "Mm-hmm" show him coasting while she monologued.
